surfaces.change: New --run-line LINE (only with --probe; refused elsewhere): the probe scaffold's purpose header gains one line, '# ' then LINE verbatim, after '# Read-only:' and before '# Bound:'. A LINE with a line break, a blank LINE or one starting '#' is refused, exit 2, nothing on stdout. Without the flag the emission is unchanged apart from the secrets note below.

The probe scaffold's placeholder comments carry a secrets note naming secret files, remote URLs and git remote -v, and one comment line that is the command `git remote -v | sed -E ...`, masking each URL password as xxx and each GitHub token's characters after its prefix as xxx.

The no-bale clipboard fallback (a request bale.toml command read at craft time) now copies what `bale clipboard --block "probe block"` copies: URL passwords and GitHub tokens masked by 0.4.59's rule, UTF-16LE with no byte-order mark for a clip.exe command, UTF-8 otherwise, through a python3 program the scaffold carries (PROBE_FALLBACK_MASK_PY). Its success line on stderr gains ', as 'bale clipboard' copies it', ' (UTF-16LE with no byte-order mark, for clip.exe)' for clip.exe, and bale's '; masked N ... before copying' aside. Without python3, or when it fails, it copies nothing and says so on stderr. The bale-on-PATH path is unchanged.
--bundle's help carries, whole on its own line: "A successor's bundle takes a stem no earlier bundle of its slug had.", followed by why.

4.2 names --run-line and the header line it writes; 4.3's Secrets-aware rule names remote URLs and git remote -v beside secret files, and the fallback paragraph says the no-bale copy is bale clipboard's copy (masked, UTF-16LE for clip.exe) and copies nothing without python3.

notes: No bale verb, exit code, record, schema or vocabulary changes. A probe crafted by 0.4.60 with a request clipboard key needs python3 for its no-bale copy; one crafted earlier keeps copying raw UTF-8, unmasked, there.
